title: Positive degree characterizes ampleness on a proper integral curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then $\mathcal N$ is ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] if and only if $\deg_k(\mathcal N)=\chi(C,\mathcal N)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)>0$, the degree of [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. No smoothness or geometric integrality hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve (applied to a proper integral curve)

proof.text: The scheme $C$ is nonempty by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Properness includes finite type and separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $C$ is a variety in the sense of [def-pc-curve]. The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $(1)$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], $\mathcal O_C$ and every invertible module are coherent: locally each is free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. Finite type over a field and properness therefore meet the Noetherian hypotheses used below.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, preliminary proper-curve and finiteness hypotheses; Properties Tag 01OV and Cohomology of Schemes Tag 01XZ

proof.text: Write $d=\deg_k(\mathcal N)$. By [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], each $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$ is invertible, including $\mathcal N^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_C$. The degree definition [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] gives $\deg_k(\mathcal O_C)=0$. Induction using [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive] gives $\deg_k(\mathcal N^{\otimes n})=nd$ for every $n\ge0$: the induction step adds $d$ to the preceding degree. Rearranging the definition of degree gives $\chi(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})=nd+\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, tensor-power degree and Euler-characteristic identities; Tag 0AYX

proof.text: First assume $\mathcal N$ ample. The field $K=\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is a finite extension of $k$ by [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety], since Step 1 showed $C$ is a proper variety. If $C$ were affine, it would be $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a one-point space of dimension zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], contrary to $\dim C=1$. Choose a point of $C$. The ampleness definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] supplies $n\ge1$ and a section $s$ with that point in the affine open $C_s$. Hence $s\ne0$ and $C_s\ne C$, since $C$ is not affine. Applying [lem-trf-curve-section-degree-positivity] to $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$ gives $nd>0$ by Step 2, whence $d>0$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, forward implication; Tag 0B40, nonzero section with a zero

proof.text: For the converse assume $d>0$. By [lem-pc-coherent-hi], the coherent modules $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$ on proper $C/k$ have finite-dimensional cohomology. Since $C$ is Noetherian of dimension one, [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] kills their cohomology in degrees above one. Thus [def-pc-euler-characteristic] and Step 2 give $h^0(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})=nd+\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)+h^1(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\ge nd+\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$, which is unbounded as $n\to\infty$. Choose any nonempty affine open $U\subseteq C$. By [lem-sc-affine-complement-finite-on-integral-curve], its complement is a finite set $\{x_1,\ldots,x_t\}$. Each $x_i$ is closed: in an integral dimension-one scheme a non-generic point with a distinct specialization would give the chain $\overline{\{y\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{x_i\}}\subsetneq C$, contrary to the dimension definition [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the generic point exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. Since $C/k$ is finite type, [lem-kun-closed-point-field] gives $[\kappa(x_i):k]<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, reverse implication, growth of sections and choice of finite boundary

proof.text: Choose $n\ge1$ with $h^0(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})>\sum_i[\kappa(x_i):k]$. Evaluation at the $x_i$ is a $k$-linear map to $\bigoplus_i(\mathcal N^{\otimes n})_{x_i}\otimes\kappa(x_i)$, whose dimension is that sum because each fibre has dimension one over $\kappa(x_i)$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. Its kernel is nonzero by the dimension inequality. Take a nonzero section $s$ in the kernel, so $s$ vanishes at every boundary point. Consequently $C_s\subseteq U$, using the fibrewise definition of $C_s$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. By [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open], $C_s=U\cap C_s$ is affine. This produces a fixed $n\ge1$ and nonzero $s\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})$ with affine nonvanishing locus. No surjectivity of the evaluation map was required.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, evaluation kernel and affine nonvanishing locus; Properties Tag 01PV

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_C$ be any quasi-coherent ideal. It is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](2), since $C$ is locally Noetherian and $\mathcal O_C$ is coherent. Put $\mathcal F_e=\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal N^{\otimes en}$ for $e\ge0$. These are coherent because locally the invertible factor is $\mathcal O_C$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. The nonzero section $s$ has nonzero generic value: on a trivializing open where it is nonzero its coefficient injects into the function field by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]. Hence its coefficient at every stalk is nonzero, by that same injection. Multiplication by $s$ on each $\mathcal F_e$ is injective: after trivializing, it is multiplication by a nonzero element on the ideal $\mathcal I_x$ in the domain $\mathcal O_{C,x}$. It is an isomorphism on $C_s$. Thus $0\to\mathcal F_e\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal F_{e+1}\to\mathcal Q_e\to0$ is exact, with coherent cokernel by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](1). Its support is contained in $C\setminus C_s$, which omits the generic point and has dimension at most zero: any strict chain there would extend by $C$ to a length-two chain [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0B5X, injective section-multiplication sequence and zero-dimensional cokernels

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support](1) to each coherent $\mathcal Q_e$ on the proper $k$-scheme $C$: Step 6 verified its support dimension at most zero, so $H^1(C,\mathcal Q_e)=0$. The long exact sequence explicitly supplied by [pqf-def-cohomology] for the short exact sequence in Step 6 gives a surjection $H^1(C,\mathcal F_e)\twoheadrightarrow H^1(C,\mathcal F_{e+1})$ for every $e\ge0$. Composing these maps shows that $H^1(C,\mathcal I)\to H^1(C,\mathcal F_e)$ is surjective for every $e$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, surjectivity on first cohomology; Cohomology of Schemes Tag 0B3J

proof.text: The vector space $H^1(C,\mathcal I)$ is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-coherent-hi], since $C/k$ is proper and $\mathcal I$ is coherent. Apply [lem-sc-section-affine-open-kills-cohomology] with $X=C$, $L=\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$, $F=\mathcal I$, and $p=1$: $C$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $L$ is invertible, and $C_s$ is affine by Step 5. Each element of a finite basis is killed by some power of multiplication by $s$. Choose $E\ge1$ at least all these exponents (take $E=1$ for the zero vector space). The map $H^1(C,\mathcal I)\to H^1(C,\mathcal F_E)$ kills the basis and hence is zero. It is also surjective by Step 7, so $H^1(C,\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal N^{\otimes En})=0$. The exponent $En$ is positive and may depend on $\mathcal I$, exactly as required.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, finite basis and eventual annihilation; Cohomology of Schemes Tag 01XR

proof.text: Step 8 applies to every quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_C$. The field $k$ is Noetherian by Step 1, $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper by hypothesis, and $\mathcal N$ is invertible. Therefore [lem-trf-ideal-twist-vanishing-implies-ample] with $R=k$ gives absolute ampleness of $\mathcal N$. Together with Step 3 this proves the equivalence, with the original degree and without imposing smoothness or geometric integrality.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, final application of Cohomology of Schemes Tag 0B5U, implication (3) => (1)

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, both directions; finite-basis and stalk-injectivity details expanded.
